name: Ed Miliband
role: Labour leader (2010–2015); Energy and Climate Change Secretary (2008–2010); Energy Security and Net Zero Secretary (2024–2026); Foreign Secretary since July 2026
summary: Soft-left Labour politician who led the party on a One Nation platform of responsible capitalism, higher taxes on top incomes, tighter regulation of energy and finance, devolution and an elected second chamber. He has spent his career on climate and energy policy, writing the Climate Change Act 2008 and later driving Clean Power 2030, Great British Energy and nuclear expansion. In foreign policy he supports NATO, the EU relationship, Trident and conditional humanitarian intervention, and as Foreign Secretary has stressed Ukraine, international law, development finance and a two-state solution.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In his 2013 social security speech he said there will always be a place for universal support 'like an NHS for all'; the 2015 manifesto he led pledged to rescue the NHS, and he voted against the 2012 GP-commissioning reforms.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led pledged to raise the minimum wage to more than £8 an hour by October 2019 and to promote the Living Wage; a rise of moderate size rather than a larger multiple.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: As Energy Secretary he argues that exposure to international fossil fuel markets leaves Britain a price-taker and that clean power must be built with public involvement; his book Go Big, per a reviewer, criticises the 'market is king' philosophy. He does not reject markets outright.

public-ownership.rationale: He voted for creating publicly owned Great British Energy and consistently for bringing the railways into public ownership as Great British Railways. Existing energy suppliers and water were not nationalised, so the record covers rail and a new energy company rather than all major utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Voted generally for raising the tax rate on income over £150,000, for a mansion tax, higher taxes on banks, capital gains tax, stamp duty and windfall taxes; the 2015 manifesto he led restored the 50p rate and funded the NHS with a mansion tax.

unions-good.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led says Labour values trade unions as an essential force for a decent society; as Energy Secretary he repeated that unions are an essential part of a modern workplace, and he defended union political funds in 2013 while reforming individual affiliation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Pledged and carried out tighter regulation: the 2015 manifesto promised a stronger energy regulator, separating the Big Six generation and supply arms, payday lender and betting limits and a bank bonus tax; as Energy Secretary he is reforming Ofgem as a consumer champion; voted for an English football regulator.

cut-welfare.rationale: He argues the welfare bill must be controlled and wants people who can work to do so, but voted almost always against reductions in welfare spending as opposition leader; as a Cabinet minister he voted for the 2024 winter fuel means test and the 2025 Universal Credit and PIP bill. Mixed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted generally for requiring mass retention of communications data and for mass surveillance powers, and for Labour's anti-terrorism laws, while voting generally against secret evidence in courts.

decide-locally.rationale: Called for reversing a century of centralisation and for an English Devolution Act; voted generally for more powers for local councils and the Scottish and Welsh parliaments, but generally against councils keeping business rates.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Signed the equal marriage pledge in 2012, saying gay and lesbian couples deserve an equal right to marry, and voted Aye at Second Reading of the Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Bill on 5 February 2013.

abortion-legal.rationale: Almost always voted for fewer obstacles to abortion access. The record covers access measures rather than a statement on the general legal framework.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: In 2014 he said Labour should fight for the traditions of England and not cede English national identity to others.

gradual-change.rationale: Argued in Go Big and interviews that he had not been bold enough and that the left should think big rather than incrementally; he works through existing institutions, so the answer is a lean only.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Pledged immigration controls and transitional controls, and voted for the 2026 Immigration and Asylum Bill second reading, but voted almost always against stricter immigration enforcement and the Rwanda and Illegal Migration bills; no clear call for lower numbers.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Backed UK military intervention in Libya and Afghanistan, supported air strikes against ISIL in Iraq in 2014, and in 2013 said action in Syria was not ruled out if conditions were met; his later votes on combat operations were mixed.

open-borders.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led says immigration needs to be properly controlled with fair rules and he promised transitional controls; he has not endorsed open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: He presents clean energy as a route to growth and jobs, describing a 'pro-growth approach' to building clean energy, and rejects the view that climate action requires limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: As Energy and Climate Change Secretary he introduced the Climate Change Act 2008 with an 80% cut by 2050; as Net Zero Secretary he launched Clean Power 2030 and Great British Energy, lifted the onshore wind ban and voted for carbon budgets and the 2026 climate orders.

expand-nuclear.rationale: As Energy Secretary he describes the government as pro-nuclear, backs Sizewell C and small modular reactors with signed contracts, and calls nuclear essential to clean power; he voted for the 2022 Nuclear Energy (Financing) Bill.

state-directs-investment.rationale: As Energy Secretary he created and funded the publicly owned Great British Energy and the National Wealth Fund to direct investment into clean energy industries and supply chains; the 2015 manifesto he led proposed a British Investment Bank.

direct-votes.rationale: Generally voted against an EU membership referendum and said it would be damaging, but the 2015 manifesto promised a referendum before any transfer of powers to Brussels and he backed the AV referendum. Mixed.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In September 2026 he told the Commons that anyone questioning Israel's right to exist as a homeland for the Jewish people is wrong and that Israel has every right to defend itself; in 2014 he said no one in Labour should question Israel's right to exist.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led promised to cut the deficit every year with no additional borrowing, but in 2011-12 he and Ed Balls proposed temporary VAT cuts and brought forward investment to boost jobs. Mixed.

national-self-determination.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led backs a viable independent state of Palestine alongside Israel; in 2026 he stressed Ukraine's sovereignty and said he stood for self-determination as a British value.

force-without-un.rationale: In the 2013 Syria debate he said that if a proper case is made there is scope in international law for action without a Chapter VII Security Council resolution, citing Kosovo; he set conditions including legal base and Commons approval.

work-for-welfare.rationale: His 2013 speech says it is wrong to be idle on benefits when you can work, and his compulsory jobs guarantee requires taking a job or losing benefits, though he stresses help to find work and recognition of those who cannot.

class-collaboration.rationale: His One Nation framing and 2015 manifesto call for an economy of mutual obligations in which employers and employees cooperate; his 2014 speech told business 'we can't do it without you'.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Implemented the manifesto ban on new North Sea licences, voted for a fracking ban and windfall taxes, and said drilling would not lower prices; the 2026 King's Speech bill included a drilling prohibition.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: In December 2012 he said integration did not require people to lose their differing identities, citing his own Jewish heritage, while stressing English; reported via a news summary.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Voted generally for scrapping the Northern Ireland Troubles conditional-immunity scheme and the ban on civil claims; his own statements on the point are not recorded.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led states that no person should suffer discrimination or a lack of opportunity; he voted generally for equality and human rights laws.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Almost always voted against more restrictive regulation of trade union activity, including strike minimum service levels; he has accepted ballot requirements in existing law and in 2026 voted for electronic ballot rules.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Voted generally for UK membership of the EU and for more EU integration; said in 2014 Britain's future lies inside the EU and as Foreign Secretary seeks a deeper strategic alliance with it. His 2015 manifesto also promised a referendum before any transfer of powers.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: As Foreign Secretary he pledged to uphold NATO and nurture the alliance with the United States, and to stand with Ukraine as long as it takes.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Voted Aye on the 2023 regulations requiring relationships and sexuality education in Northern Ireland schools.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: In 2026 he called for a new deal on debt through longer repayment, cheaper refinancing and faster restructuring, with deeper relief for a small number of countries, not general cancellation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: As Foreign Secretary he calls development central to policy, took the World Bank governor role personally and cites Gleneagles debt relief, but frames aid as partnership, and the UK has cut aid spending.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Consistently voted for replacing Trident, and the 2015 manifesto he led committed to a minimum, credible, independent nuclear capability with a continuous at-sea deterrent.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Supports a two-state solution in which Israel lives alongside a Palestinian state, which implies territorial compromise, but he has not discussed land swaps directly in the statement's terms.

collective-defense.rationale: Pledged to uphold the UK's commitment to NATO and to stand shoulder to shoulder with allies; he did not speak to the mutual-defence clause itself.

flat-income-tax.rationale: His record is for a progressive structure: the 2015 manifesto he led restored a 50p rate on incomes over £150,000, and he voted generally for higher income tax on high earners. He has not discussed a flat tax directly.

common-currency.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

ban-cartels.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led proposed separating generation and supply in the Big Six energy companies and opening their books, plus more competition on the high street.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Voted generally for requiring imported goods to meet domestic standards and for several Labour Trade Bill amendments in 2018-2021.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Voted generally for removing hereditary peers from the House of Lords and pledged an elected replacement for the Lords; this concerns the legislative seats, not titles.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led says Labour is the party of equality and that no person should suffer discrimination; in 2012 he proposed banning employers from advertising jobs to one ethnic group only.

paid-care-work.rationale: A reviewer reports that Go Big argues unpaid care work, valued at £1.2 trillion, is left out of GDP and undervalued; the book's own recommendation on pay is not clear from the review.

corporate-influence.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led pledged to cap donations, create a statutory lobbyists register, repeal the Lobbying Act and ban MPs from paid directorships; he made 'standing up to' Murdoch and energy firms a theme.

job-guarantee.rationale: Proposed a Compulsory Jobs Guarantee for people unemployed over a year (young people over 12 months, adults over two years), paid for by a bank bonus tax; targeted at long-term unemployed, not everyone willing to work.

non-intervention.rationale: In 2013 he said military intervention in Syria was not ruled out and discussed legitimate grounds for it; as Foreign Secretary he imposes sanctions and arms licence limits affecting Israel's settlement policy.

national-law-over-international.rationale: As Foreign Secretary he stresses defending international law and in 2026 changed official UK policy to follow the International Court of Justice finding that the occupation is unlawful.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Consistently voted against the 2012 reforms making GPs buy services for patients, against school autonomy and academies, and for restricting NHS services to private patients.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led says people want more say in decisions that affect their lives and that government must do things differently; in 2014 he called for a people-led constitutional convention.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: In a 2015 written Q&A he said trans rights lagged behind gay rights and that Labour would review gender identity law and policy to strengthen them; he later criticised press campaigns against trans equality.

assisted-dying.rationale: Voted for the Terminally Ill Adults bills at Third Reading in June 2025 and Second Reading in September 2026; he has publicly expressed concern about pressure on vulnerable people.

social-market-economy.rationale: Promoted 'responsible capitalism' and predistribution, calling for a market economy with fairer rules, and as Energy Secretary pairs markets with a fair transition and consumer regulation.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: As Foreign Secretary he commits to NATO and the US alliance and calls NATO a defensive alliance.

rent-control.rationale: The 2015 manifesto he led promised three-year tenancies as the norm with a ceiling on excessive rent rises. This caps increases within tenancies rather than rents in shortage areas generally.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Supported maintaining the Trident submarine deterrent, which is based in Scotland, in the 2015 manifesto and by voting to replace it.

second-chamber.rationale: Consistently voted for a wholly elected House of Lords, and as leader pledged to replace the Lords with an elected Senate of the Nations and Regions.

free-public-college.rationale: Proposed cutting tuition fees from £9,000 to £6,000 (2015 manifesto) and earlier a graduate tax, not abolishing tuition; consistently voted against higher fees.

future-generations.rationale: Wrote the legally binding Climate Change Act 2008 and says turning back on climate action would betray future generations and that climate security for future generations needs climate leadership.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Said in 2013 that the last Labour government was right to provide tax credits for those in work, pledged in 2015 not to cut them, and voted in October 2015 to reverse the tax credit cuts.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: In October 2026 he argued the global financial system and order fail developing countries, citing imbalances of power between Global North and South, and proposed reforms to debt, development bank lending and resilience finance.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Consistently voted for replacing Trident and said in 2015 that he was not for unilateral abandonment, while pursuing multilateral disarmament.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: In December 2012 he said immigrants must learn English and proposed help with English and a ban on poor English in public-facing public sector jobs; the 2015 manifesto repeats the public-facing requirement. Reported partly via a news summary.

voter-id.rationale: Generally voted against photographic voter identification at polling stations.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: In 2013 said there will always be a place for universal support (NHS, basic pension) but also that winter fuel should not go to the richest pensioners; voted in 2024 for means-testing winter fuel and later for scrapping the two-child limit. Mixed.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Reported in his 2010-2015 leadership as supporting a financial transaction tax. Taken from a reference text rather than a speech.

notes: Views shift over time: as Labour leader he said Labour would scrap ID cards (earlier he voted for them as an MP); he opposed an EU referendum then campaigned to Remain; as a Cabinet minister since 2024 he has voted for government measures such as the winter fuel means test and welfare changes that he opposed in opposition. Answers on cabinet-era votes reflect collective government decisions as well as his own statements. The TheyWorkForYou summary aggregates votes since 2005 and is used as a record, not as his own words.
